scope: Five map files, six facade image files and two ZIPs physically inspected; repeated presentations do not create additional content identities. Two later caption-only historical leads are separately recorded, not counted as inspected image files.

sources.finding: Walled City of Lahore by Uzair Baig. No model reuse licence or survey date established. Supplied filename association, not a remote pixel-hash match.
Arab Village by mawais. CC0 listing and creator clarification; uploaded archive notice instead says CC BY 3.0. Retain credit and both records.
Grassy Field by metalix; CC-BY listing. Background foliage/textures expressly excluded; comments about learning techniques do not silently replace the bundled licence.

Commercial adaptation allowed subject to applicable terms, attribution, licence link and modification notice; no added restrictions on licensed material. Not a warranty for all embedded third-party images.
Legacy BLENDER header, file-block headers, SDNA and ENDB. Parser is a bounded subset, not Blender validation.
1909 Imperial Gazetteer atlas collection. Possible source collection for the 1823 plate; exact plate match/publication provenance not established in this intake.
Indexed catalogue text supports circa-1840 Punjab Hills painting and object 1925,0406,0.2. Direct open failed; supplied image pixels not matched. Digital reproduction permission not decided.
Photograph 2005.100.491.1 (66): unknown artist, albumen silver print, 1858-61. Met marks its version Public Domain and offers Open Access. No image downloaded or exact uploaded-file match claimed.
Phillaur subsection gives sarai-to-fort conversion between 1809 and 1812 under Mokham Chand, and later British military use. Architect attribution and broader narrative not independently verified.
1839 as Ranjit death year; reproduces matching Phillaur photo title and Met accession. Limited context, not wholesale historical verification.

images.title_as_supplied: India in the time of Warren Hastings
images.observation: Approximate boundaries and a religion-based legend are visible. Preserve author categories as source metadata, not game faction or population classes. Not a precise 1792 snapshot.
Plate 22, Justus Perthes, Gotha visible. Depicted year is not publication date. British Territory and British Protected States use different legend fills. Not a surveyed 1792 boundary.

images.title_as_supplied: Uncaptioned outline on a modern Google basemap
images.observation: No legend establishing meanings of coloured outlines. Do not infer a maximal empire, an agreed game polygon, current territorial position or historic transport from these lines.

images.title_as_supplied: Empire of the Lahore Durbar, greatest extent circa 1844
images.observation: Visible author credit Navtej Singh Heer, 2015. Hatched earlier-control claim is distinct from the main extent claim. Attribution and meaning recorded, historical geometry not admitted.

Legend distinguishes locations in present-day Pakistan/India. Modern names including Faisalabad are visible. Do not backdate a modern label or city footprint; source edition and control claims unresolved.

attachment_limitations: Later image-only interruption messages supplied placeholders without distinct retrievable attachment records in this inspection. They have not been visually inspected, hashed, deduplicated or counted as new assets. Caption-based catalogue candidates are not pixel matches.
